questions.question: What is an annunciator panel in an aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: A single panel that has all the warning and condition lights for the aircraft, making it easy for pilots to monitor all the systems at a glance.

concepts.label: A single panel that has all the warning
terms: a single panel that has all the warning

concepts.label: making it easy for pilots to monitor all the systems at a glance
terms: making it easy for pilots to monitor all the systems at a glance

questions.question: What condition could cause a takeoff warning system to actuate?
questions.idealAnswer: When the throttles are advanced for takeoff and the flaps, slats, speed brakes, and elevator trim are in an unsafe condition, or not in "takeoff" configuration.

concepts.label: When the throttles are advanced for takeoff
terms: when the throttles are advanced for takeoff

concepts.label: elevator trim are in an unsafe condition
terms: elevator trim are in an unsafe condition

questions.question: What would cause the warning horn to sound when throttles are pulled back for landing?
questions.idealAnswer: When the landing gear is not down and locked for landing.

concepts.label: When the landing gear is not down
terms: when the landing gear is not down

questions.question: What is indicated by a red light in the landing gear position indication portion of the annunciator panel?
questions.idealAnswer: Gear is in an unsafe condition (" in transit" ) and not down and locked for landing.

concepts.label: Gear is in an unsafe condition
terms: gear is in an unsafe condition

questions.question: Where is the landing gear safety switch (‘squat switch’ or ‘weight on wheels switch’) normally located?
questions.idealAnswer: On one of the main landing gear shock struts so the switch is actuated when the weight of the aircraft is on the wheels.

questions.question: What info is given to a pilot to indicate that all the landing gears are down and locked?
questions.idealAnswer: Three green lights indicate that all three wheels are down and locked and is in a safe position for landing.

concepts.label: Three green lights indicate that all three wheels are down
terms: three green lights indicate that all three wheels are down

concepts.label: is in a safe position for landing
terms: is in a safe position for landing

questions.question: What part of the anti-skid system generates the anti-skid warning signal?
questions.idealAnswer: The control unit or (control box)

questions.question: How is the pilot alerted that an anti-skid system has automatically returned to the manual brake mode?
questions.idealAnswer: A warning light or a message on the aircrafts alerting system.

questions.question: What is the significance of an anti-skid warning light?
questions.idealAnswer: That the system is off or has failed.

questions.question: How does the stall warning system in a small aircraft alert the pilot of an impending stall?
questions.idealAnswer: A audible alert and or a warning light.

questions.question: What devices are used to provide warnings for a retractable landing gear system?
questions.idealAnswer: A horn or other audible device and red warning lights.

concepts.label: A horn or other audible device
terms: a horn or other audible device

questions.question: What landing gear positions must be indicated by regulations?
questions.idealAnswer: That the gear is down and locked or up and locked position.

questions.question: How does it take off configuration warning differ from a landing gear warning?
questions.idealAnswer: Takeoff warnings are usually intermittent horns and landing gear warnings are steady horns.

concepts.label: Takeoff warnings are usually intermittent horns
terms: takeoff warnings are usually intermittent horns

concepts.label: landing gear warnings are steady horns
terms: landing gear warnings are steady horns

questions.question: What is the function of a Mach airspeed warning system?
questions.idealAnswer: It alerts the pilot that VNE limit has been reached or exceeded.

questions.question: What systems are commonly used to activate the landing gear warning systems?
questions.idealAnswer: The throttles and wing flaps.

questions.question: Why do airplanes with bleed air anti-icing systems have anti-ice overheat lights?
questions.idealAnswer: To indicate an over temperature condition, usually because of a break in the bleed air duct.

concepts.label: To indicate an over temperature condition
terms: to indicate an over temperature condition

concepts.label: usually because of a break in the bleed air duct
terms: usually because of a break in the bleed air duct

questions.question: What warning system may be required when a nickel cadmium battery is installed in an aircraft?
questions.idealAnswer: A battery temperature monitoring system.

questions.question: At what time would a check of the landing gear warning system normally be made?
questions.idealAnswer: A check is made during a landing gear retraction test.

questions.question: If an aircraft with retractable landing gear has only one green light to indicate gear down and locked, how will the switches be connected? In series or parallel?
questions.idealAnswer: The switches will be connected In series.

questions.question: Where would you locate the procedures for checking and adjusting the landing gear switches?
questions.idealAnswer: In the Aircraft maintenance manual.

questions.question: What is the usual means for alerting the crew of a jet transport aircraft that the cabin doors are not properly closed?
questions.idealAnswer: A warning light.

questions.question: Why are transport category aircraft equipped with a master caution and warning system?
questions.idealAnswer: They alert the crew that a malfunction has occurred and corrective action is required.

concepts.label: They alert the crew that a malfunction has occurred
terms: they alert the crew that a malfunction has occurred
